title: The Widest Tornado Ever Recorded Was 2.6 Miles Across

scenes.text: The widest tornado ever recorded was 2.6 miles across.
It hit El Reno, Oklahoma, on May 31st, 2013.
Radar measured it 2.6 miles wide. That's 4.2 kilometres.
Mobile radar also clocked winds of 296 miles an hour, 500 feet above the ground.
It was first rated EF-3. Then it was upgraded to EF-5, the top of the scale.
Two point six miles wide. The widest ever recorded.

description:
The tornado that struck El Reno, Oklahoma, on May 31, 2013 was 2.6 miles (4.2 km) wide, the widest tornado ever recorded.
Mobile radar measured winds of 296 mph about 500 feet above the ground. It was first rated EF-3 and later upgraded to EF-5.
How far from a storm would you feel safe?
first_comment: Note: the wind speed was measured by radar above ground, not by the damage on it. Would you have guessed a tornado could be this wide?
